related_questions.question: What organ controls your blood pressure?
How will kidney function affect your blood pressure?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, the kidneys play a crucial role in regulating blood pressure.

list.title: Sodium and Water Balance:
list.snippet: The kidneys control the amount of sodium and water in the body. When blood pressure is too high, the kidneys excrete more sodium and water in the urine, reducing blood volume and lowering pressure. Conversely, when blood pressure is too low, the kidneys retain sodium and water, increasing blood volume and raising pressure.

list.title: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS):
list.snippet: The kidneys produce an enzyme called renin, which triggers a cascade of events that lead to the release of the hormone aldosterone. Aldosterone promotes sodium reabsorption in the kidneys, increasing blood volume and blood pressure.

list.title: Blood Vessel Diameter:
list.snippet: The kidneys can also regulate blood vessel diameter. When blood pressure is low, the kidneys release substances that dilate blood vessels, allowing more blood to flow and lowering pressure. Conversely, when blood pressure is high, the kidneys constrict blood vessels, reducing blood flow and raising pressure.

list.title: Filtering and Excreting Waste Products:
list.snippet: The kidneys remove waste products from the blood, including toxins and excess electrolytes. This helps maintain a healthy fluid balance and blood pressure.
